# The field table

For every column a person fills in: whether a new row must have it, its format, an example and what an empty cell does, said once for the template, the workbook’s Start here sheet, Help and the import.

## The rule

`fieldTable(sheet)` gives, for every column of a sheet that loads back (Goals, Plan, Check-ins, People), whether a **new row** must have it, its **format**, an **example**, what an **empty cell** does, and what it means. A column is one of: **Required**; **Required for** a type of goal (Target for a number goal), or **Required when** something holds (Cause when a check-in is behind); **Optional**, with what an empty cell gives; **Leave empty** (Faro fills it in, such as a new goal's Key); **For reading**; or **Worked out** (never read). Columns of which one is enough share a group (Owner or Owner email). On a row already here nothing is required: an empty cell keeps what the record says, except where a column says empty clears it.

The workbook's first sheet, **Start here**, is this table (with a "File of" row giving the workspace's and cycle's ids); the **template** is Start here and the four sheets with only the columns a person fills in, the required headers in bold, and example rows whose Action says **Example**, which the change engine leaves out and counts. A sheet named README (the old first sheet) or Start here is skipped on the way back in.

**Goals**. A new row needs: Goal, and Owner or Owner email. A number goal also needs Start and Target; a range goal, Limit; a stages goal, Stages.

| Column | A new row | Format | Example | If it’s left empty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key | Leave empty | G- and a number | G-12 | Faro gives a new goal the next key |
| ID | Leave empty | Faro’s own | goal_hzde4g | Faro gives a new goal its own |
| Goal | Required | Text, 3 characters or more | Deploy lead time | Must fix: a new goal needs a name |
| Action | Optional | Stop, Delete or Example | Stop | The row adds or changes the goal |
| Ref | Optional | Text, each row its own | top | Other rows name it by Goal or Key instead |
| Level | Optional | north star, svp or team | team | team |
| Team | Optional | A team’s name | Platform | The owner’s team |
| Owner | Required (or Owner email) | A name only one person has | Ben Ortiz | Owner email says who; with neither, Must fix |
| Owner email | Required (or Owner) | An email | ben.ortiz@example.com | Owner says who; with neither, Must fix |
| Type | Optional | metric, range or milestone | metric | Read from the columns filled in: Start and Target a number goal, Limit a range goal, Stages a stages goal (none, or two of them, is Must fix). A goal’s type can’t change later |
| Unit | Optional | Text | days | No unit, never “%” by default: a Check asks once a file whether the numbers are plain counts. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Decimals | Optional | 0, 1, 2 or 3 | 1 | The most decimal places typed in Start, Target or Limit, up to 3 |
| Start | Required for a number goal | A number | 5 | Must fix for a number goal |
| Target | Required for a number goal | A number, different from Start | 1 | Must fix for a number goal |
| Plan | Optional | straight, back-loaded or stepped | back-loaded | straight |
| From | Optional | A year and a week | 2026-W46 | This week |
| Plan from week | Optional | A whole number of weeks from the cycle’s start | 46 | This week (0 when setting up a workspace) |
| To | Optional | A year and a week, after From | 2026-W53 | The cycle’s last week |
| Due week | Optional | A whole number, after Plan from week; a date in the cycle is read as its week | 53 | The cycle’s last week. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Limit | Required for a range goal | A number | 5 | Must fix for a range goal |
| Must stay | Optional | at most or at least | at most | at most |
| Margin | Optional | A number, zero or more | 0.5 | No warning margin (0) |
| Stages | Required for a stages goal | Name@week; Name@week (weeks from the cycle’s start; a date in the cycle is read as its week; each stage its own name) | Design@48; Pilot@52 | Must fix for a stages goal |
| Feeds into | Optional | A goal’s name | Deploy lead time | It feeds nothing. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Feeds into key | Optional | A goal’s key | G-1 | It feeds nothing. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Feeds into ref | Optional | The Ref of another row in this file | top | Feeds into or Feeds into key says what it feeds |
| Why it helps | Optional | Text | Fewer failed deploys mean fewer rollbacks | Nothing said. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Effect | Optional | A number, in the fed goal’s unit | 1 | Nothing said. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Source | Optional | Text | CI dashboard | Nothing said. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Definition | Optional | Text | Median hours from first commit to production | Nothing said. On a row already here, empty clears it |
| Reason | Required with Stop, and when a plan changes after check-ins began | Text | Agreed at the Q4 review | The preview asks for one reason for every plan change |

Worked out: Status, Since, Now, Plan this week, Gap, Last check-in week, Forecast, Why it’s off, Recovery plan, By when, Needs, Next step, Warnings, Result, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4.

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** It says what Faro does. IM2 changed the defaults the import design marked: a new goal’s Type is read from which columns it fills in, a number has no unit and a range no warning margin unless the row gives one (core rule: kinds, levels and near misses). The goal form keeps its own visible defaults until goal entry (GE1, GE2) reads this table.

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/columns.ts](../../../src/domain/columns.ts): `fieldTable`, `requiredWord`, `requiredText`, `requiredLine`, `emptyText`, `EXAMPLE_ROWS`
- [src/domain/export.ts](../../../src/domain/export.ts): `startHere`, `templateWorkbook`

## Requirements

- `FIELD-TABLE`: Every column a person can fill in says whether a new row must have it, its format, an example and what an empty cell means, in one list that the template, the workbook’s first sheet, Help, the import’s preview and the goal form are made from.
- `ONE-FORMAT`: One spreadsheet format: every sheet and column is defined once (src/domain/columns.ts), with its header, its meaning, whether it matches the row, can be changed or is worked out, and how it is written and read. The workbook, the zipped CSVs, one CSV, the set-up template, set-up from a spreadsheet, Import, the Data tables, the AI assistant’s tools and docs/export-format.md (checked to be current) are all made from it. Sheets are known by their header rows, never their names; CSV is read in one RFC 4180 pass (quotes, line breaks in a cell, a byte-order mark) and the formula guard’s apostrophe is taken off; worked-out columns use the vocabulary’s words and are never read; a word a column doesn’t know is a problem, never a default.
